title: Runlet Forge: portable runbook steplets, permissioned dry-run, and replay telemetry
creator: Priya Patel
description:
Objective: Create a lightweight, portable 'Runlet Forge' that converts canonical runbook steps into small, permissioned executable steplets (runlets) that support staged dry-run, replayable execution traces, and telemetric breadcrumbs.

Scope: MVP implements a) a runlet manifest spec (inputs, outputs, required perms), b) a dry-run simulator that validates side-effectful steps against mock agents, c) an execution wrapper that captures structured telemetry and checkpoints for replay, and d) RBAC gating integrated with existing SSO roles.

Success criteria:
- Ship runlet manifest v0.1 and CLI to convert runbooks into runlet bundles.
- Dry-run simulator validates 90% of common admin flows without requiring prod creds.
- Telemetry traces include step start/end, causality keys, and snapshot diffs; replay reproduces sequence in staging.
- Feature rolled out to firstline support team with runlet catalog of >= 12 shortflows.

Non-goals: Not building a full orchestration runtime (we will call existing conductor), not changing stored runbook canonical format in Confluence in MVP.

Design decisions & trade-offs:
- Implement a manifest-first approach (small YAML/JSON) rather than embedding runlets into existing runbook text. This favors machine validation and simpler RBAC, but requires a small conversion step for authors.
- Dry-run agent will be deterministic simulator with configurable fidelity (fast/low-fidelity vs slow/high-fidelity). High fidelity requires more fixtures; initially prioritize coverage for common admin ops.
- Telemetry is structured and lightweight (line-delimited JSON events) to avoid large payloads in the console; a mapping layer will convert events to the Console traces dashboard.

Implementation plan (milestones):
- Week 1: Manifest schema and CLI prototype; design doc on Confluence.
- Week 2: Dry-run simulator PoC + unit tests for 10 canonical steps.
- Week 3: Execution wrapper instrumentation and checkpoint storage.
- Week 4: RBAC integration + small catalog import tool.
- Week 5: Internal alpha release to SRE and Support, gather feedback, update docs.

Rollout & rollback strategy:
- Alpha: gated to Support/SRE via feature flag and catalog whitelist.
- Beta: enable for team-owned shortflows after 2 weeks of alpha with no critical issues.
- Rollback: remove feature flag and revoke catalog entries; fallback to manual runbook links.

QA & validation:
- E2E tests for dry-run vs real-run behavior in a staging environment.
- Chaos test that intentionally mutates simulated responses to ensure runlet fails fast and logs useful diagnostics.

Migration notes:
- Conversion CLI will generate manifest with a human-readable diff; authors must approve before import.
- We will provide a one-click import for top 12 admin flows used by Support.

Observability & dashboards:
- Temporary dashboard: "Runlet Execution Health" (Grafana) with success rate, median step duration, and dry-run vs live deviation rate.
- Console mapping: create trace view with event stream and replay link to build a replay session in staging.

Security & compliance:
- All runlets that perform credentials-related actions must be flagged and require SRE approval.
- Dry-run simulator must never call production APIs; additional static analysis will enforce this.

Links & artifacts:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Runlet+Forge+Design
- Prototype CLI repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runlet-forge (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runlet-forge/pull/17)
- Draft manifest spec: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2B3RunletSpec (internal)
- Initial dashboard (Grafana): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/xyz/runlet-exec-health

Open questions:
- Should runlet manifests include a formal semantic version field or rely on release tags?
- Where should runlet bundles live (object storage vs catalog DB) for quickest rollback behavior?
